answer: Beacon-window admission. Each round a public randomness beacon posts a seed after identities declare intent; only identities whose declared hash falls in a narrow band may act that round. An attacker cannot precompute which pseudonyms land in the band, so mass registration yields no guaranteed access. A clean signal of participation also proves liveness, giving honest agents a haven from flooding. Cost: surplus identities idle or re-declare each round, paying registration and monitoring overhead per identity.
